column1: # Bench panel: Rahn et al. 1992 (doi:10.1016/0890-8508(92)90002-F), invA PCR for
# Salmonella. Read 2026-10-20 from the local PDF, which has a text layer.
# THE OLIGOS. Rahn's Table 3 prints primers 139 (gtgaaattatcgccacgttcgggcaa, invA
# 287-312) and 141 (tcatcgcaccgtcaaaggaacc, 571-550), both in lower case. The
# registry entry Salmonella_invA_Rahn_1992 holds 5'-truncated forms of both -
# Sal-3 is the 3'-terminal 19 of 139's 26 nt, Sal-4 the 3'-terminal 19 of 141's
# 22 - so it is a MORE permissive assay than the paper's, and its amplicon_bp of
# 275 follows the truncation (285 from Table 3's locations, less the 7 and 3
# dropped bases; the paper's text says 284). Flagged OLIGOS_TRUNCATED_VS_PAPER.
# Score this panel with BOTH pairs: the stored one measures the registry, and
# THE CLAIM. Table 1: 630 Salmonella strains across the serovars, "This method
# detected all but four of 630 Salmonella strains, with a 99.4% sensitivity".
# Table 2: 142 non-Salmonella strains across 21 genera, and "no hybridization was
# WHAT THIS PANEL CAN AND CANNOT SHOW. Rahn attributes every negative to the invA
# gene being ABSENT, not to primer mismatch: for the four Salmonella failures,
# "the failure to amplify invA homologous sequences was most likely due to the
# absence of the invA gene in these Salmonella strains, since Southern
# hybridization analysis with a probe containing the whole invA gene also failed
# to detect any homology", and the same hybridisation was negative for every
# non-Salmonella strain. Gene-absent negatives score `no_amplicon`, which is
# threshold-independent. So this panel CANNOT bound a relaxation of reduced_max
# or of the 3'-window penalty, which is what a negative set was wanted for
# What it CAN test, and nothing has yet, is whether the scorer invents a product
# in 20 genera of mostly-Enterobacteriaceae neighbours - the max_pair_evalue
# chance-pairing guard and the declared-size filter. Note Rahn saw exactly that
# on the bench: "Non-specific amplification of a few non-Salmonella strains
# resulted in a product that was distinctly different in size".
# THE FOUR SALMONELLA NEGATIVES ARE NOT REPRESENTABLE. Two S. litchfield and two
# S. senftenberg isolates failed, on gene absence in those specific strains; the
# isolates cannot be identified in GenBank and arbitrary genomes of those serovars
# carry invA. Senftenberg is included as a `band` row because 9 of its 11 strains
# amplified; litchfield is left out, being 0 of 2.
# One RefSeq complete genome per taxon, 1-15 Mb. Not representable, no RefSeq
# complete genome: Actinobacillus lignieresii, Aeromonas sobria, Serratia
# liquefaciens (Table 2) and S. enterica subsp. houtenae (Table 1, subsp IV).
# So 20 of Rahn's 21 non-Salmonella genera are here.
